questionText: Once the DBMS informs the user that a transaction has been successfully completed, its effect should persist even if the system crashes before all its changes are reflected on disk. This property is called
explanation:
Durability guarantees that once a transaction is committed, its effects are saved permanently in non-volatile storage and will persist even in the event of a power outage or system crash.

Overview of ACID Properties:
• Atomicity: Ensures that all operations within a transaction are completed successfully; otherwise, the transaction is aborted entirely.
• Consistency: Ensures that a transaction transitions the database from one valid state to another while preserving all database rules and invariants.
• Isolation: Ensures that concurrent execution of transactions leaves the database in the same state as if they were executed sequentially.
• Durability: Guarantees that the changes of a committed transaction survive any system crash.
